claim_scope: Project-status publishing and a synthetic OKR example only; no collectors, incident delivery, agent monitoring, credential changes, or remediation are implemented.

events.evidence: HTTPS returned 200; the live HTML, templates, status JSON, and trace matched the checked-in bytes.
events.summary: The public dashboard explains the security and OKR chore families and serves downloadable synthetic profile and event templates.
events.title: Personal OKR extension published

events.evidence: The test suite builds the OKR example and preserves its progress, performer, reviewer, and next-review fields.
events.summary: A synthetic objective and three key-result lanes use the same validated JSON and Perfetto pipeline as the public project status.
events.title: Personal OKR status example exercises the shared pipeline

events.evidence: HTTPS returned 200 and the live trace digest matched the generated status document.
events.summary: The read-only dashboard reports Chores security work without claiming to monitor agents or deliver incident reports.
events.title: Public security project status deployed

events.evidence: The test suite rebuilds both artifacts and reads the trace with Perfetto's trace processor.
events.summary: One validated profile and event stream now produce a machine-readable status document and a deterministic Perfetto activity trace.
events.title: Status exporter produces JSON and Perfetto views

events.evidence: The projection boundary is part of the public format contract.
events.summary: Private status must use its own profile, events, outputs, and deployment credentials rather than a redacted public artifact.
events.title: Private data requires a separate projection

events.evidence: The versioned profile, event, and status schemas define the public status contract.
events.summary: A project profile and ordered event stream are the authored inputs for JSON status and Perfetto views.
events.title: Public project status format defined

events.evidence: No scheduler, lease service, reviewer workflow, or agent identity registry is present.
events.summary: Agent assignment and independent review must not delay or suppress direct human reporting of suspected unauthorized activity.
events.title: Routine rotation remains a research question

events.evidence: The repository contains no collector or remote-execution path.
events.summary: No failed-service, listening-socket, update, storage, backup, or monitoring-health check runs from the public status publisher.
events.title: Read-only security checks remain outside the prototype

events.evidence: No incident receiver, delivery transport, or acknowledgement endpoint is present.
events.summary: A dashboard is not an urgent notifier and cannot establish that an owner received or acknowledged a report.
events.title: Direct owner reporting requires a tested delivery path

events.evidence: The project README defines the security goal, the reporting duty, and the current implementation limits.
events.summary: Routine security checks may rotate, but every agent must immediately report suspected unauthorized activity, including its own, directly to the human owner.
events.title: Chores defines proactive agent security hygiene

summary: Incident-motivated agent security hygiene, with a reusable personal OKR status example.
